clue.text: Fabulous city appeared reluctant to lose hospital

parts.note: came means appeared, turned up

indicators.note: to lose tells us a letter is dropped from the word meaning reluctant

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, reluctant
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs

explanation.surface: A legendary city seemed unwilling to give up its hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's court of legend, so a city from fable rather than history.

clue.text: Rare voices not trained in a music school

indicators.note: trained means the letters are disciplined into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unusual untrained voices turning up at an academy of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not trained' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is part of the fodder and 'trained' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatoire is a college for training professional musicians.

clue.text: Gulls nicked picture

parts.note: to gull is to dupe, and mugs are dupes or gullible people
hot is slang for stolen, nicked

explanation.surface: Seabirds were caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Gulls looks like seabirds, but it means people who are easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a police photograph of a suspect's face, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Plant parasite almost covering edge of allotment

indicators.note: covering means the shortened parasite wraps around the edge letter
almost means the parasite loses its last letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

indicators.note: edge of picks out the final letter of allotment

explanation.surface: A pest has nearly overrun the border of a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering aquatic plant.

clue.text: Essay about a very English saint that's nothing like the real thing

indicators.note: about means the attempt goes around the other pieces

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: An essay about a deeply English saint bears no resemblance to the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay is a verb-noun meaning attempt, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, a distorted mockery of the genuine article.

clue.text: Centre of labyrinth guarded by Cretan king's children

indicators.note: guarded by means the central letter sits inside, protected by, the king's name

parts.note: Minos was the mythical king of Crete; the 's is no letter here

indicators.note: Centre of picks out the single middle letter of labyrinth

explanation.surface: The heart of the maze was watched over by the offspring of the Cretan king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Minotaur's labyrinth, built for King Minos; R, the middle letter of LABYRINTH, goes inside MINOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Minors are people under legal age, that is, children.

clue.text: Complaint of young man in springtime

indicators.note: in places the young man inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A youth falls ill in the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Game providing business opportunity

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players stake on horse cards
a fresh area of trade where goods can be sold

explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is also an English horse-racing town; the card game takes its name from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a card game, and a new market is a fresh commercial opening.

clue.text: Get rid of manuscript removed from chambers by solicitor

indicators.note: removed from means the manuscript letters are taken out of the chambers word

parts.note: chambers are rooms
a tout solicits custom, so is literally one who solicits

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes away a document from his office to destroy it.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor suggests a lawyer, as do chambers, but it is a tout soliciting business.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out is to find and eradicate something completely.

clue.text: Almost everyone's too full for starters in the evening

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the words too and full

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody has eaten so much they can't manage a first course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the onset of darkness, the coming of evening.

clue.text: Yarn by fine writer

parts.note: wool is spun yarn
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A thread produced by a skilled author.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia Woolf was an English novelist of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf is a famous novelist, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Extract from thank you letter temporarily?

definitions.meaning: a typical line thanking someone for a gift
for now, for the time being

explanation.walkthrough: In a thank-you letter one writes thanks for a gift; the same words mean for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for now, and present also means a gift being thanked for.

clue.text: Spirit shown by eastern army getting back to front

indicators.note: getting back to front means the final letter of the army word is moved to its start

parts.note: a host is a great army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: An eastern army regaining the front line shows real morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding character of a group.

clue.text: Undertaking to finish at any time in recital

indicators.note: in recital means the words are spoken aloud, so we want what they sound like

parts.note: end means finish and ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A promise to wrap up whenever, made during a concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, END EVER sounds like the answer; the surface's 'recital' looks musical but signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or enterprise, a venture one undertakes.

clue.text: See heart of city in Country Life?

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: in places the central letters inside the country name

parts.note: Italy is a country

indicators.note: heart of picks out the two central letters of city

explanation.surface: Readers are urged to look at an urban feature in a glossy rural magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Country Life is a long-running British magazine about country houses and rural living; here the words split, Country giving ITALY and Life the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitality means liveliness or energy, the quality of being full of life.

clue.text: Country celebrates historic events

parts.note: land means a country or nation
to mark an occasion is to celebrate it

explanation.surface: A nation commemorates its important past occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Landmarks are turning points or significant events in history.

clue.text: Drawing in front of steam vessel

indicators.note: in front of places the steam letter before the boat

parts.note: S stands for steam, as in SS for steamship
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture produced ahead of a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing made quickly.

clue.text: Native American ceremony in US can end in a state

indicators.note: in a state means agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: America may finish up in one of its states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like a US state but means in a flustered mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun Dance is a religious ceremony of Plains Native American peoples.

clue.text: Singer last to go outside church for dance music

indicators.note: outside means the shortened singer wraps around the church letters
last to go means the final letter of the singer is dropped

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist is the final one to leave the church grounds for a disco.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music with a fast repetitive beat.

clue.text: Author taking care of short bit of writing

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for care of, as on envelopes

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the writing is cut off

parts.note: a letter is a bit of writing

explanation.surface: A writer takes trouble over a brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: Colette was a French novelist, author of Gigi.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette was a celebrated French writer, so an example of an author.

clue.text: Flatter mountain goat?

definitions.meaning: to flatter is to praise someone insincerely to win favour
a goat that butts things is a butter, and one on a mountain is up

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a goat butts, so it is a butter, and a mountain goat is one that is up high.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is an idiom for flattering them to gain favour.

clue.text: Cotton on a reel is woven

indicators.note: woven means the letters are interlaced into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Thread on a spool is spun into fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Cotton looks like the thread, but 'cotton on' is an idiom for understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is to grasp or understand, the same as realising.

clue.text: See about new lead for our old beagle

indicators.note: about means the sighting word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to spy is to see

indicators.note: lead for picks out the first letter of our

explanation.surface: Check out the new lead for our elderly hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The beagle is Charlie Brown's dog in the Peanuts comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoopy is the famous cartoon beagle of Peanuts, an example of the breed.

clue.text: Unlucky break of Emil Nolde

indicators.note: break of means the letters of the painter's name are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Misfortune struck when the German painter Emil Nolde took a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Emil Nolde was a German Expressionist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-omened means attended by bad omens, hence unlucky or doomed.

clue.text: Insufficient foliage in desert?

indicators.note: Insufficient means the foliage word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: leaves are a plant's foliage

explanation.surface: Barely any greenery grows in the arid wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon, so to go away from, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Speaker's circuits stop being effective

indicators.note: Speaker's means as said by a speaker, so we want the sound of the word

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: A presenter's racetrack loops cease to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To lapse is to expire or become invalid, ceasing to have effect.

clue.text: Log cabin's first from American heartland

indicators.note: from means the cabin's initial is taken away from the American word

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre, spelt the American way

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of cabin's

explanation.surface: A wooden hut originally hailing from the middle of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log cabin' reads as one phrase, but Log is the definition, in the sense of recording something.
explanation.definitionFit: To log data is to record it, that is, to enter it in a record.

clue.text: Connoisseur in swimming pool with Heine

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of pool and the poet's name move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert takes a dip in the pool with the German poet Heinrich Heine.
explanation.walkthrough: Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German poet.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wines.

clue.text: Miserable maiden without doubt missing one

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: missing means the letter for one is lost from the word for without doubt

parts.note: easily means without doubt, as in easily the best
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unhappy young woman, certainly short of a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means paltry or meagre, contemptibly small, a sense of miserable.

clue.text: Most appropriate situation for building block

definitions.meaning: being in your ... is being in the setting that suits you best
a basic constituent part of something larger

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is from the idiom 'in one's element'.
explanation.definitionFit: Element means both a natural milieu and a fundamental component.
